{"results":{"id":"guideline.compose-or-propose","type":"guideline","title":"Compose or propose","summary":"Compose a new interface need from tokens and existing components first, and open an issue or RFC only when the system itself has to change.","tags":["composition","contribution","governance","rfc"],"links":{"related":["pattern.action-hierarchy","component.button","component.badge"]},"status":"stable","file":"guidelines/compose-or-propose.md","body":"Most interface needs are met by composing what the system already publishes. Change the system
only when composition cannot express the need without copying or overriding a component.

## Compose first

Work through these in order and stop at the first one that meets the need:

1. A published variant, size, or parameter of an existing component.
2. Existing components placed together in product markup, such as a Badge beside a Button or a
   Link after an action group.
3. Product layout and chrome styled with semantic tokens. Use a primitive token only when no
   semantic role expresses the choice.

A composition that meets the need stays in product code. It does not need an issue, a record, or
a review.

## Do not fork a component

Composition stops being composition when product code rebuilds what a component owns. Do not:

- Copy a component's styles or structure to make a variant that the contract does not publish.
- Restyle a component's internal parts, or override the tokens it reads, to create a variant,
  state, or size the contract does not publish.
- Define component tokens in product code.
- Use one component to do another's job, such as a Badge as a control or a Link styled as a
  Button. The action hierarchy pattern says which control fits which job.
- Rebuild a component's states, focus ring, or accessible name handling in a new element.

When one of these is the only way to meet the need, the system is missing something. Propose it.

## Propose a change

Open an issue on the design system when the change fits the components and tokens it already has:

- A variant, size, or parameter on an existing component.
- A bug in a component, one of its implementations, a token, or its documentation.
- A composition used in more than one place that should become a pattern.
- A new component whose behavior comes from a standard platform control plus tokens, such as an
  icon or a field shell.

Some changes alter how the system works, not only what it contains. Say so in the issue, so the
design question is settled before anyone writes code:

- A component that owns focus management, an overlay, or a composite keyboard model, such as a
  Dialog, Select, Menu, or Tabs.
- A new token tier, or a semantic role category that does not exist yet.","sections":["compose-first","do-not-fork-a-component","propose-a-change"]}}

{"results":{"id":"pattern.form-field","type":"pattern","title":"Form field","summary":"Give every form control the same label, hint, error, required, disabled, and form behavior.","tags":["form","field","label","error","validation"],"status":"stable","file":"patterns/form-field.md","body":"Text field, Text area, Select, Checkbox, Switch, and Radio group share the guidance below. Each
component record keeps only the rules about its own control, such as what its value is.

## Label

Provide a visible label that names the value. The label is the control's accessible name.
Placeholder text is not a label. Write "Email address", not "Enter email".

## Hint

Use a hint for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state. The hint is
associated with the control, so assistive technology reads it as the description.

## Error

Write the error as what to fix: "Enter an email address with an @ sign", not "Invalid".

- A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
- Clear the error when the person edits the value. A form reset restores the value but leaves the
  error, so clear it on reset too.
- While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
- The error is associated with the control, so assistive technology reads it as the description.
- The invalid state always includes the text message. Meaning never depends on color alone.

## Required

A required control is announced as required, and shows it by more than color. A required control
with no value blocks its form from submitting.

## Disabled

Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard, and a disabled control submits nothing.
When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.

## Form value

Inside a form, the control's value submits under its name, and reset restores the initial value.
Each component says what its value is, such as the checked option of a Radio group.

## Focus

Keyboard focus stays visible in every state, including under forced colors.

## Switch and forms

Switch applies its setting immediately, without a separate submit action. It can also submit with a
form, so the guidance on this page applies to it. Use Checkbox when the choice takes effect only
when the form is submitted.","sections":["label","hint","error","required","disabled","form-value","focus","switch-and-forms"]}}

**Taproot doesn't have a date picker or calendar component.** Text field is the closest fit, but it only collects typed dates: its `type` options are `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `url` and `tel`, with no `date`.

**What I'd use for now:** a Text field with `type="text"`, following `pattern.form-field`:
- **Label:** name the value, such as "Check-in date".
- **Hint:** show the format, such as "Use the format DD/MM/YYYY".
- **Error:** say what to fix, such as "Enter a check-in date after today".
- **Validation:** check the date in your form code, because Text field doesn't parse dates or limit their range.

**If guests choose from a known list:** when the booking only has a small set of available dates, use Select instead, or Radio group if the list is short enough to show in full.

**If you need the calendar popup:** this has to be proposed as a new component, per `guideline.compose-or-propose`. A date picker owns an overlay, focus management and a composite keyboard model, so the issue should say that it changes how the system works. That way the design gets settled before anyone writes code.

Dialog isn't a shortcut, because it would only provide the overlay. You'd still have to build the calendar grid and its keyboard behaviour yourself, without a Taproot contract behind them. If you need the popup before Taproot has one, a third-party picker or custom build would sit outside the system, so it's best to raise that in the issue too.

{"components": ["component.text-field"]}
